notes: Three repositories that are one piece of work: a rules-engine API, a web UI that authors rule sets and tries them, and a Playwright Test project that tests both through fixtures, page objects and data-driven cases. Sessions run in this order because each builds on the previous repository's working tree. Ports: API 4400, web 4410. Nothing is pushed anywhere.

sessions.name: rules-api
sessions.goal: A TypeScript rules-engine service: rule sets as JSON, evaluated over a payload through HTTP, with unit tests, an audit log, and a README whose commands are proven by running them.
sessions.level2:
Windows 11, PowerShell 7, Node 20 or newer, npm. The repository is C:\Projects\rules-api and it is empty apart from README.md. Express 4 with TypeScript, zod for validation, tsx for running TypeScript, node's built-in test runner for tests (`npm test` runs `tsx --test` over `src/**/*.test.ts`). The service binds 127.0.0.1:4400. Rule sets live as one JSON file each under data/rulesets/ and are tracked; the audit log data/audit.jsonl is not tracked.

Rules for every task here:
- Write the .gitignore before the first `npm install`. The runner commits what a task leaves behind.
- Never leave a server running. Start it with `$p = Start-Process -FilePath node -ArgumentList 'dist/main.js' -PassThru -WorkingDirectory C:\Projects\rules-api`, wait for the port with a bounded loop (at most 60 seconds), call it, and stop it in the same step's `finally` with `taskkill /PID $p.Id /T /F`. Never `Start-Process npx` or `Start-Process npm` by bare name: PowerShell hands the .ps1 shim to the Windows shell and nothing starts.
- Nothing interactive. No `npm init` without `-y`, no generators that ask questions.
- Errors from the API are JSON of the shape { "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } } with the HTTP status that fits; validation errors add "issues".
- Do not touch any other repository.

tasks.title: api-scaffold
tasks.prompt:
Create the service project by hand in C:\Projects\rules-api.

1. First, before installing anything, write C:\Projects\rules-api\.gitignore with one entry per line: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `*.log`, `data/audit.jsonl`, `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`.
2. `npm init -y`, then install express, zod as dependencies and typescript, tsx, @types/node, @types/express as dev dependencies. Pin what npm installs (no caret ranges) so a later install reproduces this one.
3. tsconfig.json: strict, target ES2022, module NodeNext, moduleResolution NodeNext, outDir dist, rootDir src, include src.
4. src/main.ts starts an Express app on 127.0.0.1:4400 with `GET /health` answering 200 `{ "ok": true, "service": "rules-api" }`. Keep the app in src/app.ts (a function that builds and returns the Express app without listening) so tests can mount it on an ephemeral port; main.ts only listens.
5. package.json scripts: `build` = `tsc -p tsconfig.json`, `start` = `node dist/main.js`, `dev` = `tsx src/main.ts`, `test` = `tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`, `typecheck` = `tsc --noEmit`.
6. One test, src/app.test.ts, that builds the app, listens on port 0, fetches /health, asserts the body, and closes the server.
7. Prove it: `npm run build`, `npm test`, and one bounded step that starts dist/main.js, fetches http://127.0.0.1:4400/health, prints the body, and stops the process tree in `finally`.
tasks.expected: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `npm test` pass; GET /health on 4400 answers the JSON above; node_modules and dist are not tracked.

vcs.commitMessage:
Scaffold the rules-api service

Express and TypeScript by hand, an app factory apart from the listener so tests can mount it on an ephemeral port, and a health endpoint proven by calling it.

tasks.title: rule-model-and-evaluator
tasks.prompt:
Add the rules model and a pure evaluator, with unit tests, in C:\Projects\rules-api. No HTTP in this task.

1. src/rules/model.ts: zod schemas and inferred types.
   - RuleSet: id (slug: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens), name, version (positive integer), rules (array).
   - Rule: id (slug, unique within the set), name, priority (integer, higher runs first), when (Condition), then (Action[], at least one).
   - Condition is one of: a leaf `{ "field": "applicant.age", "op": ..., "value": ... }` with ops eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, in, contains, exists; a group `{ "all": [Condition...] }`; a group `{ "any": [Condition...] }`. Groups nest. `field` is a dotted path into the payload. `in` expects an array value; `contains` works on strings and arrays; `exists` ignores value.
   - Action is one of: `{ "type": "set", "path": "output.rate", "value": ... }`, `{ "type": "tag", "tag": "vip" }`, `{ "type": "reject", "code": "underage", "message": "..." }`.
2. src/rules/evaluate.ts: `evaluate(ruleSet, payload)` returns `{ output, tags, matched, rejected }`: output starts as a deep copy of the payload and `set` actions write into it by path (creating objects along the way); tags is a de-duplicated array in the order added; matched lists `{ ruleId, name }` in evaluation order; rejected is `{ code, message }` or undefined. Rules run by priority descending, ties in array order. The first `reject` action stops evaluation: later rules do not run, and the rejecting rule is the last in matched. A missing field makes every op except `exists` false. Comparisons with gt/gte/lt/lte apply to numbers only; anything else is false, never a throw.
3. Unit tests in src/rules/evaluate.test.ts and src/rules/model.test.ts: at least 14 cases covering every op, a nested all/any group, priority ordering, tag de-duplication, set creating nested paths, reject stopping evaluation, a missing field, a non-number compared with gt, and two model rejections (duplicate rule id, unknown op) with the zod issue path shown.
4. Run `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` and put the counts in the summary.
tasks.expected: `npm test` passes with at least 14 tests across the two new files; the evaluator is pure (no file or network access) and never throws on a well-formed rule set.

vcs.commitMessage:
Add the rules model and a pure evaluator

zod schemas for rule sets, rules, nested conditions and actions, and an evaluator that runs rules by priority, writes set actions by path, collects tags and stops at the first reject.

checks.name: there are at least 15 tests in total

tasks.title: rulesets-store-and-http
tasks.prompt:
Expose rule sets and evaluation over HTTP in C:\Projects\rules-api, backed by JSON files.

1. Store: src/store/fileStore.ts reads and writes one file per rule set at data/rulesets/<id>.json, atomically (write to a temp file, then rename). List, get, put, delete.
2. Seed data/rulesets/loan-approval.json (tracked in git): id loan-approval, name "Loan approval", version 1, and these rules in this order: `underage` (priority 100): reject with code underage when applicant.age lt 18; `unsupported-country` (priority 90): reject with code unsupported_country when applicant.country not in ["BG", "DE", "RO"] (express it with the ops available); `vip` (priority 50): tag vip when applicant.income gte 100000; `rate-small` (priority 10): set output.rate to 0.12 when loan.amount lt 5000; `rate-large` (priority 10): set output.rate to 0.08 when loan.amount gte 5000.
3. Routes, mounted by src/app.ts: `GET /rulesets` (array of { id, name, version, rules: <count> }), `GET /rulesets/:id` (the full set, 404 with code not_found), `PUT /rulesets/:id` (body validated with the RuleSet schema; the id in the path must equal the id in the body, else 400 with code id_mismatch; validation failures are 400 with code invalid_ruleset and `issues` as zod reports them; answers 200 with the stored set), `DELETE /rulesets/:id` (204, or 404), `POST /rulesets/:id/evaluate` (body is the payload object; answers 200 with the evaluation result plus `ruleSetId` and `version`; 404 when the set is missing; 400 with code invalid_payload when the body is not a JSON object). Every evaluation appends one line to data/audit.jsonl: { at, ruleSetId, version, matched: [ids], rejected: code or null }.
4. Tests in src/http/routes.test.ts that mount the app on an ephemeral port against a temporary copy of the data folder (never the tracked seed): list contains loan-approval; get 404; put an invalid set and assert code invalid_ruleset with a non-empty issues array; put a valid set, get it back, delete it, get 404; evaluate the seed with an underage applicant (rejected underage, rate absent), with a VIP from DE borrowing 7000 (tag vip, output.rate 0.08, not rejected), and with a payload that is an array (400 invalid_payload). At least 8 new tests.
5. `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, and one bounded step that builds, starts dist/main.js, calls GET /rulesets and POST /rulesets/loan-approval/evaluate with a valid applicant, prints both bodies, and stops the process tree in `finally`. Confirm data/audit.jsonl gained a line and is ignored by git.
tasks.expected: All routes above answer as specified; the seed set evaluates the three example payloads as described; `npm test` passes; data/audit.jsonl exists after an evaluation and `git status` does not list it.

vcs.commitMessage:
Store rule sets as JSON files and expose them over HTTP

CRUD on rule sets, evaluation with an audit line per call, a seed loan-approval set, and route tests against a temporary data folder.

tasks.prompt:

sessions.name: rules-tests
sessions.goal: A Playwright Test project that tests the API through request fixtures and the UI through page objects, with data-driven cases, tags, and a config that starts both applications itself.
sessions.level2:
Windows 11, PowerShell 7, Node 20 or newer, npm. The repository is C:\Projects\rules-tests and it is empty apart from README.md. @playwright/test with TypeScript; the browser is Chromium only. The applications under test are C:\Projects\rules-api (port 4400, `npm run build` then `npm start`, README.md documents the routes) and C:\Projects\rules-web (port 4410, `npm run build` then `npm start`, every interactive element has a data-testid; the web-smoke task's summary and the .tsx files list them). Rules for every task here:
- Write the .gitignore before the first `npm install`: node_modules/, test-results/, playwright-report/, blob-report/, .env, .env.*.
- The Playwright config starts both applications through `webServer` entries with `cwd` set to each repository, `reuseExistingServer: true`, and a `url` to wait on (the API's /health, the web app's /). - Never leave a server running: Playwright stops what its webServer started; anything you start yourself you stop in the same step. Never `Start-Process npx` or `Start-Process npm` by bare name.
- Nothing interactive. `npx playwright install chromium` is allowed; it is a download.
- Do not touch any other repository.
